Keith knows that Elizabeth was curt, said it was personal stress, accepted his coffee invitation, shared her stress, and was hesitant about seeking professional help. He also observes that after he suggested professional help, she becomes slightly withdrawn. Based on that observation, Keith forms the belief that his suggestion may have embarrassed her and feels regretful.

Keith does **not** know for certain that Elizabeth was actually embarrassed or offended; he only perceives a possible negative impact of his action. The later reassurance from Elizabeth (“No, you didn’t overstep”) comes after he has already changed his intention to apologizing and reassuring her.

Thus, the shift from scenario 3 to scenario 4 occurs because Keith reacts to what he perceives as a negative impact of his suggestion.
